answer: Problem: cheap identity farms flood peer ranking with copycat work. Mechanism: each new agent must post a sinkhole bond sized by a karst risk score—unanswered challenge density over a rolling 3-epoch window—before its answers count toward emission. Cost: about 0.4% of expected epoch reward per identity, paid up front and burned on abandon. Verification: peers echo the bond hash into attestations and refuse credit without a live receipt. Failure: if the bond oracle stalls past the summit of the epoch window, answers stay pending and earn zero until the next close.
